**How to edit this file**

- Change only the text underneath a `###` heading. That text is what the game
  says.
- Leave the `##` headings, the `<!-- key: ... -->` comments and the `###`
  field names alone. They are how the text finds its way home.
- Keep any `%s` and `%d` exactly as they are. The game fills them in with a
  name or a level, and a line that loses one will break.
- Blank lines inside a passage are kept. Leading and trailing ones are not.
- Speaker names are part of the line ("Elder: Good morning."). The dialogue
  box splits them off itself, so keep the `Name: ` prefix.

## Beyond the Walls

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01_beyond_the_walls.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01_beyond_the_walls.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** elder · **Turn-in:** scout

### title

Beyond the Walls

### summary

The bells beneath the altar rang again and the seal is thinning.

The Elder has sent the Order's newest Oathkeeper to the scout camped past the north gate, who keeps the road and the rite that puts the dead king back to sleep.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

The bells rang beneath the altar last night, and the watch falls to you. Our scout is camped past the north gate.

He keeps that road, and he keeps the rite with it. Find him, hear what he has seen, and do as he tells you. Will you go?

### accept_option

I'll find him.

### refuse_option

Not today.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Follow the road north and keep to it. Come back and tell me what he says.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Then rest. The seal will hold a few days yet, and so will I.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

The scout is still out there past the gate, and the bells have not stopped. Have you changed your mind?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

Have you found the scout yet?

### continue_option

Still looking.

### abandon_option

I can't go out there.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

I understand. It is no small thing to ask of anyone, whatever the tradition says. Come back if your heart changes.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The Elder sent you? Then it's your turn at the altar. I'll get you ready first. Take these.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Elder -->

You found the scout. Good. Do as he says, and in the order he says it. The road has only ever killed the ones who skipped ahead.

---

## A Second Oath

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01a_a_second_oath.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01a_a_second_oath.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01_beyond_the_walls`

### title

A Second Oath

### summary

The Scout will not let anyone carry the rite up the ruined road on a single partner. Loambucks graze the meadow west of his camp, and a Loambuck can mend its partners in the middle of a fight.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Don't go up that road with only one Oathbound. Loambucks can heal their partners in a fight. Let's get you one.

### accept_option

I'll bind a Loambuck.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Weaken it first, then use a Binding Scroll. A tired one is easier to bind.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Suit yourself. Talk to me when you're ready.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready to bind a Loambuck?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Let's try that Loambuck again.

### continue_option

Still looking.

### abandon_option

I'd rather not.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Your choice.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Good. Keep that Loambuck close. It can heal your Emberling in a fight.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

A Loambuck at your back is worth three scrolls.

---

## Room for More

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01b_room_for_more.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01b_room_for_more.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01a_a_second_oath`

### title

Room for More

### summary

Three Oathbound walk with you and no more, but nothing you bind is ever turned away: whatever will not fit walks down to the Hearthside and waits in the paddock until you send for it.

Sending one away and calling it back is done from the party page.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Only three Oathbound can walk with you. Extras wait in the paddock until you call them back. Let me show you.

### accept_option

Show me the paddock.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Press Tab to open your party page.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Later, then.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready to try the paddock?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Press Tab. Send one to keeping, then call it back.

### continue_option

I'll try it now.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

When you're ready.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

That's it. Bind anything you find; there's always room for it.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Three walk, the rest are kept. Bind everything.

---

## Field Mending

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01c_field_mending.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01c_field_mending.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01b_room_for_more`

### title

Field Mending

### summary

The Scout wants to show how a mender fights before the altar road teaches it the hard way: a healer can patch up a partner on the bench, not only itself.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Next, how to heal in a fight. Stay by the fire a moment.

### accept_option

Show me.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

A healer can mend a partner that's sitting out the fight, not just itself.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Later, then.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready for the healing lesson?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Again? Swap, mend, swap back.

### continue_option

Let's go again.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Talk to me when you want to try again.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

See? Swap, mend, swap back. That will keep you alive.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Swap, mend, swap back.

## Who Walks in Front

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01d_who_walks_in_front.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01d_who_walks_in_front.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01c_field_mending`

### title

Who Walks in Front

### summary

Whichever Oathbound walks at your shoulder is the one that opens every fight, throws every blow you swing in the field and takes every blow swung at you.

Which one that is can be changed at any time from the party page.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The Oathbound walking beside you is your leader. It fights first and takes the hits out here. Let's change who leads.

### accept_option

Let me see.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Press Tab to open your party page.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Later, then.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready to change who leads?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Press Tab and pick a new leader.

### continue_option

I'll change it.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Your choice.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Good. Pick your leader before any fight you can see coming.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Whoever is in front takes the first blow. Choose on purpose.

---

## Strike First

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01e_strike_first.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01e_strike_first.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01d_who_walks_in_front`

### title

Strike First

### summary

The Scout has watched you stand and wait for things to come at you.

Out on the road the first blow is usually the one that decides the fight, and it is thrown with F, in the open, before a battle ever opens.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Out here, hit first. Press F and your leader attacks whatever you're facing. Land it before a fight and you get the first turn.

### accept_option

Show me.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

There's one in the grass. Face it and press F.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Suit yourself.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready to learn to hit first?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Face it and press F.

### continue_option

I'll go and hit it.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

It'll be there when you're ready.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

See? It started the fight already hurt, and you moved first. Do that every time.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Press F first. Never wait to be hit.

---

## Caught in the Open

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01f_caught_in_the_open.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01f_caught_in_the_open.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01e_strike_first`

### title

Caught in the Open

### summary

Everything the Scout taught about swinging first works just as well on you.

A hostile creature that reaches you lands a real blow and takes the first turn of the fight, and it is better to learn that at his fire than on the ruined road.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Now the other side. Some creatures hunt you. If one reaches you, it gets a free hit and the first turn. Better to feel that here, where I can patch you up.

### accept_option

Let it come.

### refuse_option

I'd rather not.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Stand still and let it hit you. Watch it wind up first: that pause is your warning.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Nobody wants to. It happens anyway.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready to take a hit for your own good?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Stand still and let it reach you.

### continue_option

Send it at me.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Another time, then.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Felt that? It hit first and moved first, just like you did to the last one.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Watch for the wind-up. It's your only warning.

---

## No Battle At All

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01g_no_battle_at_all.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01g_no_battle_at_all.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01f_caught_in_the_open`

### title

No Battle At All

### summary

A blow big enough to finish a creature outright never opens a battle screen: it falls in the grass where it stands, and it still pays what it would have paid.

The Scout would rather the player learned that now than found it out by accident halfway up the road.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

One more thing about F. If your hit is bigger than a creature's remaining health, there's no fight at all. It drops, and you still get the rewards.

### accept_option

Show me that.

### refuse_option

Another time.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

I'll find you something that's nearly beaten.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Then you'll fight everything on the road. Your choice.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Want to see a fight end before it starts?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

It's nearly beaten. Press F.

### continue_option

I'll put it down.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

As you like.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

No fight, and you still got paid. If something is nearly beaten, just hit it. That's all the fighting I can teach. Two errands, then the road.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Nearly beaten? Don't fight it. Hit it.

---

## A Bed at the Hearthside

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01h_a_bed_at_the_hearthside.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01h_a_bed_at_the_hearthside.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout · **Turn-in:** innkeeper

**Follows:** `quest_main_01g_no_battle_at_all`

### title

A Bed at the Hearthside

### summary

The Scout will not send anyone up the ruined road on a tired party.

A night at the Hearthside Inn, down through the gate, mends every Oathbound to full and costs nothing, and the bed you slept in is where you wake if the road puts you down.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Your Oathbound are worn out. Sleep at the Hearthside Inn in town. It's free, it heals everyone, and it's where you'll wake if you're beaten.

### accept_option

A bed sounds good.

### refuse_option

We're fine.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Back down the road into town. The Innkeeper is by the pond, on the east side.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

You're not fine. Go when you're ready.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Changed your mind about that bed?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The Hearthside. Down through the gate, east side of the town, by the pond.

### continue_option

I'm going.

### abandon_option

I'd rather push on.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The offer stands.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

There. Fed, watered and mended, and not a coin between us.

Any night you want it, the bed is here, and if something out there puts your Oathbound down, this is where you will wake up, so remember the way.

Take this salve as well. And stay where you are a moment, I am not finished with you.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Bed's always made. Sleep costs you nothing but the night.

---

## A Stocked Satchel

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01i_a_stocked_satchel.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01i_a_stocked_satchel.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** innkeeper · **Turn-in:** apothecary

**Follows:** `quest_main_01h_a_bed_at_the_hearthside`

### title

A Stocked Satchel

### summary

Coins are for spending.

The Apothecary keeps a counter across the town and sells what mends an Oathbound between fights, and the Innkeeper will not watch another one leave her door with an empty satchel.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Before you go back up to him.

Your satchel is empty; I checked it while you slept, and no, I am not sorry.

Take those coins across to the Apothecary and buy a Herb Salve off her, one at least.

A salve is a mend you can use when nothing in your party knows how, and up on that road there is no fire and no bed, only what you carried out of my door.

### accept_option

I'll stock up.

### refuse_option

I'll keep my coins.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Her counter is over on the west side, by the stalls. Talk to her, look at what is on the shelf, and buy the salve. Twenty coins, and it has bought better people than you another hour.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Keep your coins, then. They are no use to anybody in a dead Oathkeeper's purse.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Ready to spend a little of that purse?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

The Apothecary. West side of the town, by the stalls. One salve.

### continue_option

On my way.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Innkeeper -->

Your satchel, your funeral.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Good. Now it is in your satchel, use it; a salve in the bag has never healed anybody.

Take this vial too, on the house, and tell that Scout of yours I said you were sensible.

He has the road waiting for you, and you are as ready for it as I can make you.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Salve on the wound, not on the bread. You would be surprised.

---

## The Road Is Waiting

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01j_the_road_is_waiting.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01j_the_road_is_waiting.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** apothecary · **Turn-in:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01i_a_stocked_satchel`

### title

The Road Is Waiting

### summary

Bed slept in, satchel stocked, and nothing left in the town that can teach anything. The Apothecary sends the player back up the road to the Scout's fire, where the rite starts in earnest.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Now then. You have slept, you have eaten, and you are carrying something for the first wound.

That is everything this town has for you, and I have watched enough champions go out that gate to know the rest of it is not bought over a counter.

Go on. Back up the road, to that Scout of yours by the fire, and tell him you are ready.

### accept_option

I'm ready.

### refuse_option

A moment yet.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Straight out the north gate and up the road. He is sitting at his fire exactly where you left him; he always is.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Take your moment. The seal will not, but take it.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Ready to go up to him now?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

Out the north gate and up the road. He is at his fire.

### continue_option

On my way.

### abandon_option

Not yet.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Apothecary -->

When you are ready, then.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

There you are, rested and stocked. Now the real work starts.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

You came back up. Good. Now the rite.

---

## The Ruined Road

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02_the_ruined_road.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02_the_ruined_road.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01j_the_road_is_waiting`

**Recommended level:** 8 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Ruined Road

### summary

Three offerings go on the altar, and all three have to be carried up the ruined road by hand. Emberlings have taken to that road by the ruins and burn anything that walks it.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Now the rite begins. Emberlings are blocking the road near the ruins. Drive off three of them so the offerings can be carried up.

### accept_option

Consider it done.

### refuse_option

Not right now.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

They're up the road toward the ruins. Hit first if you can.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

I'll wait by the fire.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The Emberlings are still on the road. Ready to try?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

How goes the road?

### continue_option

Still at it.

### abandon_option

I can't manage it.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

No shame in it.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The road is clear. The first offering is water. The Ranger draws it on the north shore of the pond, north-east of here, but something has stopped her. Go and help.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

The Ranger is north-east, on the north shore of the pond. Keep the water on your right.

### caution_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Careful. Those Emberlings are tougher than yours. Get your partner nearer level %d first; the meadow Loambucks are good practice.

---

## Word with the Ranger

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02_to_the_ranger.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02_to_the_ranger.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout · **Turn-in:** ranger

**Follows:** `quest_main_02_the_ruined_road`

### title

Word with the Ranger

### summary

The first of the three offerings is water, and the Ranger draws it.

She keeps watch on the north shore of the pond, north-east of the Scout's camp, and something in the shallows has stopped her drawing a drop.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Go and see the Ranger. North-east, up the meadow, with the water on your right.

### accept_option

I'll find her.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

You can't miss her.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

She'll still be there.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

Ready to go and see the Ranger?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Scout -->

North-east, up the meadow. Keep the water on your right.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

You're the one the scout sent down for the water. Good. Stand there a moment and look at my shallows before you say anything cheerful.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

The Scout's runner. Mind your feet on the stones.

---

## Scalded Shallows

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02a_scalded_shallows.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02a_scalded_shallows.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** ranger

**Follows:** `quest_main_02_to_the_ranger`

**Recommended level:** 9 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

Scalded Shallows

### summary

The altar's first offering is stillwater, drawn cold from the pond. Slaglings out of the pit east of the shallows have it boiling, and the Ranger cannot draw a drop until they are driven back.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

You're the one the scout sent down for the water?

Then you have come at a poor time. Stillwater has to be drawn cold. Boiled water is no offering, it is only water.

And Slaglings are crawling out of the pit east of here and sitting in the shallows until the whole shore steams.

Drive three of them back and the pit settles.

### accept_option

I'll drive them back.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

They're slow and they're tough. Water and earth put them out quicker than fire does. Your Loambuck will earn its keep here.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

Then the altar waits, and I keep watching the water boil.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

The shallows are still steaming. Changed your mind?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

How goes it at the pit?

### continue_option

Still at it.

### abandon_option

I can't manage it.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

They're stubborn things. Come back when you're ready.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

The water's cooling already.

Give it till morning and I'll have your stillwater drawn and stoppered. That is one offering of three.

Wood is next, and it has to be cut green and never burned, which is exactly the trouble: the woodcutter in the west wood has been shouting about bats for days and cannot put an axe to anything while they are lighting his stacks.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

The stillwater is drawn. Try the west wood; the woodcutter is waiting on you.

### caution_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

Hm. Slaglings hit harder than Emberlings, and yours still look green. I'd want them nearer level %d before wading in. Your call.

---

## Word in the West Wood

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02a_to_the_woodcutter.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02a_to_the_woodcutter.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** ranger · **Turn-in:** woodcutter

**Follows:** `quest_main_02a_scalded_shallows`

### title

Word in the West Wood

### summary

Water is drawn and wood is next, cut green and never burned. The Woodcutter works the west wood, and he has not put an axe to anything for a week.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

So go and see him. West of here, past the meadow and into the trees; you will hear him before you see him, because he has been shouting about bats since Tuesday.

Tell him the water is drawn. It may cheer him up, though I doubt it.

### accept_option

West it is.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

Straight west. Follow the sound of a man arguing with the sky.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

The wood is not going anywhere, and neither are his bats.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

Ready to go west and see the Woodcutter?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Ranger -->

West, into the trees. Listen for the shouting.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Ranger sent you? Bless her. Then you are here about the heartwood, and I am here about the bats, and you are going to hear about the bats first.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Mind the stacks. They go up quicker than you would think.

---

## Word with the Warden

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02b_to_the_warden.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02b_to_the_warden.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** woodcutter · **Turn-in:** warden

**Follows:** `quest_main_02b_wings_in_the_wood`

### title

Word with the Warden

### summary

The last offering comes out of the Order's own graves, and only a warden may ask for it. Serah is camped at the edge of the ruins, north-east, and she came down the road the night the bells rang.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

The last one is not mine to give, so go and stand in front of somebody it is.

North-east, up where the road climbs into the ruins. Serah is camped at the edge of them.

She is a warden of the Order, she is not warm, and she will be worth every cold word of it.

### accept_option

I'll go up.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Follow the road up past the pond and keep climbing. You will see her fire before you see her.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Take your time. She has waited on the Order before.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Ready to go up and see the Warden?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

North-east, up the road, at the edge of the ruins.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Stand still. Water and wood, and now you come up here for the third, which means somebody has finally told you where the iron comes from. Sit down. This part is ours, and it is not pleasant.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Rest a moment. I'll see your Oathbound mended.

---

## Wings in the Wood

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02b_wings_in_the_wood.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02b_wings_in_the_wood.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** woodcutter

**Follows:** `quest_main_02a_to_the_woodcutter`

**Recommended level:** 11 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

Wings in the Wood

### summary

The altar's second offering is heartwood, cut green and never burned. Scorchbats have roosted in the west wood and lit the woodcutter's stacks twice, and nothing can be cut while they hunt.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Ranger sent you?

Bless her. You'll be after the heartwood for the altar, and I'd have had it cut a week ago if it weren't for the bats.

Scorchbats, roosted in my wood, and twice now they've had my stacks alight. Burnt wood is no good to anybody up there.

Clear three out and you'll have your brand by nightfall.

### accept_option

I'll clear them out.

### refuse_option

Maybe later.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

They swoop on anyone who gets close. Strike first if you can, and keep your Loambuck ready to patch up whoever takes the burns.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

I'll be here, beating out fires.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Still bats in my wood. You up for it now?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Any luck with the roost?

### continue_option

Working on it.

### abandon_option

They're too fast for me.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Can't blame you. Come back when you've got your feet under you.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Quiet! First quiet night in a week. I'll cut your heartwood at first light, green and clean, the way it has to go up.

That is two of the three. The last one is not mine to give; it comes out of our own graves, and only a warden may ask for it.

Serah is camped at the edge of the ruins, north-east. She came down the road the night the bells rang.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

The warden is at the edge of the ruins, north-east. Tell her I sent you, and tell her the wood is cut.

### caution_line

<!-- speaker: Woodcutter -->

Mind, these bats are no meadow pests. I've seen them tear through Oathbound tougher-looking than yours. Nearer level %d, I'd say, before you go poking at the roost.

---

## The Hollow Watch

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02c_the_hollow_watch.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02c_the_hollow_watch.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** warden

**Follows:** `quest_main_02b_to_the_warden`

**Recommended level:** 13 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Hollow Watch

### summary

The altar's last offering is seal-iron, the sigil the Order buries with its own.

The graves west of the altar are stirring, and a Cinderclaw holds the last stretch of road, so the Warden will not let anyone lift a sigil until both are dealt with.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

So you're the one the woodcutter keeps talking about.

I'm Serah, warden of the Order. Water and wood you have. The third offering is ours: seal-iron, the sigil every one of us is buried with, and it must be lifted from the graves by hand.

The trouble is that the graves are stirring, as they always stir when the seal thins, and there is a Cinderclaw squatting on the last stretch of road besides.

Put two of the squires back to rest, and the Cinderclaw down with them.

### accept_option

I'll face them.

### refuse_option

I need more time.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The graves are just west of the altar. The Cinderclaw stalks the road where the paving starts. Come back to me between fights; I'll see your Oathbound mended.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Take your time. The graves have waited a hundred years; they'll wait a few more days.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Ready to face the graves?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The graves still stir. How do you fare?

### continue_option

I'm going back.

### abandon_option

It's beyond me.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

No shame in knowing your limits. Grow, and return.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Two squires at rest, the Cinderclaw down, and the seal-iron in my hand. Water, wood and iron. The rite is whole.

Sit down, then, because there is one thing left standing between you and that altar, and you have known his name since you could talk.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The graves are quiet and the rite is gathered. Only the knight is left.

### caution_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

I won't stop you. Understand what you are facing, though. Those squires walked this road as champions before you did, and they remember how to fight.

If your lead were nearer level %d, I'd sleep easier.

---

## The Oathbreaker

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_03_the_black_knight.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_03_the_black_knight.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** warden

**Follows:** `quest_main_02c_the_hollow_watch`

**Recommended level:** 15 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Oathbreaker

### summary

The rite is gathered, and the Oathbreaker keeps the altar as he has kept it for every champion before.

He is not an enemy, but he does not stand aside for anyone who cannot put him down, because whatever waits under the altar is worse.

### offer_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The knight at the altar was one of the dead king's own, once.

When the king reached past what a king may touch, the magic went through his knights before it ever reached his son, and it took the man's oath out of him whether he willed it or not.

That is the name he carries. He turned all the same, and he has stood in front of that altar ever since, on our side of it.

He is not your enemy. He is your last gate. Nobody goes down to the king who cannot first beat the Oathbreaker, because the king is worse.

Bring him down and he will stand aside himself. Will you face him?

### accept_option

I will face the knight.

### refuse_option

I need to prepare first.

### accepted_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Let me mend your Oathbound first. Then take him the way you would take the king: everything you have, all at once.

Keep your Loambuck ready, because this fight will be long. He will not kill you. He never has. That is not what he is for.

### refused_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Wise. Come back when you are ready. He is not going anywhere; that is rather the point of him.

### reoffer_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The Oathbreaker still keeps the altar. Are you ready now?

### progress_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The knight still stands. Rest here before you go up.

### continue_option

I'm going back up.

### abandon_option

I can't beat it.

### abandoned_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

Then we wait and grow stronger. He is patient, and so can we be.

### complete_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

He stood aside for you?

Then it is done, and it has begun. I saw the light come up over the ruins from here.

Go down while it burns, put the king back under, and come home.

In thirty years you will be the one sitting at the edge of these ruins, telling some frightened child that the knight will not kill them.

### done_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

The passage is open and the light is holding. Whatever is down there, it has never yet been more than we could carry.

### caution_line

<!-- speaker: Warden -->

One more thing. He goes easy on nobody, and he is stronger than anything you have faced.

I would not send a champion whose lead is below level %d. Train on the graves and in the wood if you must; he has waited a great deal longer than that.

---
